Label: 14-day window and 60-day gap logic for identifying SCT dates from claims
Definition (Validated from Protocol): The patient-level SCT dataset contains processed dates for AUTO, ALLO, and CART transplants. For AUTO SCTs: (1) Group claims into 14-day windows starting from the earliest claim date. The actual SCT date is the LAST claim in the 14-day window (not the first -- first claims are workup activity). (2) All selected SCT dates must be at least 60 days apart. Claims within 60 days of a selected date are skipped. (3) If the 14-day window overlaps with the 180-day tandem boundary from the previous selected SCT, then select the claim date closest to the 180-day mark instead of the last date. This adjustment allows tandem AUTO SCTs to be appropriately captured. For ALLO and CART: Each distinct claim date is a separate event (no windowing or gap logic).
Additional Notes (Validated from Protoco: Protocol Section 5: 'Tandem SCTs are two SCTs >=60 to <=180 days apart. These are considered planned and a continuation of the line of therapy.' The 14-day window for claims processing is an implementation detail. Protocol footnote 1: 'SCTs must be within 60 days after the end of the induction or maintenance regimen to be considered a continuation of the LOT. This 60-day rule was recommended by Optum's KOL (Dr Allan Stawis) and informed by Charalampous et al.'s findings that the median time from end of induction to transplant was 33 days (IQR=27-42).'
